report:
PASS for the precise retained conditional partial scope. The operator construction, target-EP-to-equation implication, local reference conversion, conditional cardinality reduction, and after-EP normalization transport are correct. This does not establish singular EP or close P16.1. E remains the explicit antecedent of the cardinality implication; all-point fiber constancy and countable global C1 remain separate missing gates. Neither pending author result nor documentary observations were used as mathematical background.

The retained domain is an algebraically closed trivially valued field of characteristic zero, a reduced irreducible projective variety, and an actual ample rational line bundle L. The relevant BJ constructions allow singular varieties. The multilinear extension in BJ7.14 supplies the test-containing pairing used in BJ7.18; positivity, PL density, and the constant test produce the genuine Radon operator. Its model coefficients retain every b_E, and its raw mass is V=(L^n). Thus MA_raw=V MA_BJ, E_raw=V E_BJ, and E_raw-dual(μ)=V E_BJ-dual(μ/V). BJ9.20 applies because X is irreducible: finite dual energy is equivalent to integrability of every actual E1 potential. No support restriction is introduced. These are statements about the published operator, not an assigned inverse measure. [BJ](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4)

Under target EP, BJ5.11 gives compactness of the normalized target PSH space in the divisorial topology. The maximizing sequence has bounded J by BJ9.15–9.16. Its convergent subnet has an actual normalized PSH limit, and lower semicontinuity of J puts that limit in E1. BJ9.19 gives target-measure L1 convergence; energy upper semicontinuity then proves attainment of the variational supremum. Applying the PL variation estimate with both f and −f identifies the maximizing potential’s probability MA with μ/V, hence its raw MA with μ. This establishes an actual solution, rather than only convergence of measures. Irreducibility gives uniqueness modulo constants through BJ10.4. Genuine finite-energy locality and comparison are available before EP.

The supplied sign corrections are mathematically harmless and correct. The absolute-value identity is |a−b|=2(max(a,b)−b)−(a−b). The weighted integral is the test-containing pairing minus the zero-test pairing, at both finite stages and the limit. For continuous directions, the error is |t|ε on each side before division by t; the derivative follows by taking the PL derivative first and then sending ε to zero. For locality’s limiting step, the appropriate weighted convergence result is BJ7.21(ii); the source’s reference to BJ7.19(iii) there is a harmless cross-reference slip.

Continuous base change has the required fixed reference. BJ3.9 literally places Hdom(L) inside H(L) for the same actual ample rational bundle, and BJ4.16 supplies uniform approximation without EP. Consequently BE7.14 applies to the corresponding fixed-bundle metrics. The smooth regularized FS formulas pull back with their real weights unchanged. BE8.3(iv) preserves the fundamental cycle and the raw measure at each smooth stage; BE8.4 and continuity of pushforward on compact analytic spaces pass the identity to continuous metrics. BE8.18, including its dimension-zero induction and relatively regular section argument, and BJ7.23 identify this operator with the energy-pairing operator. No probability factor, component multiplicity, or reference change is lost. [BE](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.01016v3)

The local conversion also preserves the actual reference. For two valid pairs, choose a smaller positive rational δ and an index beyond both original indices and the ample-cone tail for that δ. This proves directedness. Adding zero in the ample difference class preserves the scalar potential. In section frames, h_A≥0 because the constant branch 1 occurs, so the raw weights decrease as the index increases and δ decreases. Their limit is φ+h_M, including at −∞.

The required compact neighborhoods can be obtained directly: choose affine algebra generators g_a and radii R_a in exp(Q) strictly exceeding their values at the tested point. The simultaneous inequalities |g_a|≤R_a define a compact seminorm space, by closedness inside a product of bounded intervals; the strict inequalities give an ordinary open neighborhood of the point. This does not assert strict affinoidness over the trivial field. The reference weights are finite and bounded there. Clearing rational tensor powers makes the section ratios regular functions in the original frames. Every appended original generator branch and constant floor can be placed strictly below the old finite minimum on all of Q.

For the fixed-pair approximation, a safe verification of BJ3.10 interpolates ω+D toward ω+H by ω+(1−t)D+tH, followed by rational approximation. This avoids relying on the printed interpolation ω+D+tH. The summable shifts in the argument then give the asserted decreasing sequence. Flattening requires no minimum closure: strictly shifted finite continuous majorants are ordered by pointwise domination, and compactness supplies a common upper index. Two harmless clarifications make the application fully literal. One may use the whole real-weight affine FS family, which is stable under real constants; alternatively the same compact proof uses positive rational shifts throughout and retains rational weights. At a −∞ limit, use an arbitrary finite threshold R instead of an expression such as −∞+ε. These clarifications preserve the construction and its conclusion. The local result supplies neither all-point fiber constancy nor original singular global PSH membership.

For cardinality, the normalization and its finite algebra structure, gluing data, and inverse on a dense open descend together with X, L, and the finite obstacle. Faithful flatness preserves integrality downward and descends normality. A finite normal birational algebra inside the common fraction field equals the integral closure: every element integral over the smaller algebra is also integral over that normal algebra. Descent therefore retains the actual normalization and the original possibly nonnormal X. Universal-homeomorphism descent and the local normalization definition give geometric unibranchness of X0. Thus the conditional E applies with its exact field, variety, and actual-bundle hypotheses. [Normality descent](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/033G), [universal-homeomorphism descent](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CEX)

Restriction is surjective for every analytic point. The radius-one Gauss norm on H(x)(T) is multiplicative and unchanged on H(x); with an infinite transcendence basis, every polynomial still uses finitely many variables. After completion, valuation extension to an algebraic closure can be chosen without changing this real-valued norm. Indeed, a dominating valuation ring restricts to the original valuation ring, and the finite-extension value-group bound embeds each algebraic extension group into the divisible hull of the original real value group. Completing again preserves the embeddings. The embedded k is trivially valued: a monic equation with nonzero constant term rules out both norms greater than one and norms less than one. Evaluation into this complete field gives the required norm-preserving lift.

Each finite Hdom(L) competitor has an actual same-mL section representation. Only its finitely many coefficients need enter its own larger countable field k2. The finite-cover equalizer proves section base change, and faithful flatness descends the vanishing of the evaluation cokernel. Restriction surjectivity transfers the obstacle inequality. The pulled-back envelope is continuous, genuine, and bounded, hence E1 on k2 without EP there. Continuous raw pushforward transfers the nonnegative orthogonality integral. BJ10.6 then gives domination on this irreducible competitor variety without assuming EP or inverse-equation existence there. No common countable field is assigned to an arbitrary family.

For an arbitrary PSH competitor q≤f, the decreasing compact superlevel sets {h_j≥f+ε} have empty intersection, so an entire tail is empty. Rational shifts remain in Hdom(L). The finite-competitor argument yields q≤ψ+ε, and then q≤ψ. Feasibility gives the exact target envelope identity. PL density, the envelope Lipschitz bound, and genuine uniform closure extend this to continuous obstacles; BJ5.17 supplies EP. Rational ample classes approaching a real ample class from above give the final extension by BJ5.9 and varying-class closure. This proves E implies arbitrary-cardinality EP, while preserving E as an unproved antecedent.

Normalization transport is used only after the target approaching classes have EP. Every (1+1/m)ω satisfies the strict-from-above hypothesis of BJ5.13. Its onto PSH pullback, together with exact normalization energy identities, gives onto E1 pullback, including unbounded potentials. The finite birational normalization has generic degree one, so ν_*[Xν]=[X] and the volume remains V. Its analytic homeomorphism transports integrals and dual energy, while BJ7.19 gives genuine raw pushforward for E1 potentials. In dimension zero, X is one point, V=1, the energy is the scalar potential, and the raw measure is the unit point mass. No positive-dimensional estimate is used in that case.

BJ7.1, 7.2, 7.7 and 7.8: On a reduced projective variety X of dimension n over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, the algebraic energy pairing for ample classes has a unique increasing upper semicontinuous extension to PSH tuples, given by the infimum over Hdom majorants and continuous along decreasing nets. For ω ample and V=(ω^n), Eω(φ)=(ω,φ)^(n+1)/((n+1)V) is increasing, concave, upper semicontinuous, translation-equivariant and decreasing-net continuous. E1(ω)={φ∈PSH(ω):Eω(φ)>−∞} contains bounded potentials and is upward closed within PSH(ω). Pullback to the normalization preserves the pairing and energy, and detects finite energy.

BJ7.14, 7.18, 7.19 and 7.21: For a reduced projective variety X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, the finite-energy pairing extends multilinearly to differences of finite-energy potentials. It defines unique mixed signed Radon measures through the PL test pairing; nef psh inputs give positive measures. Their mass is the mixed intersection number, their model coefficients include ord_E(X0), and they commute with normalization pushforward and decreasing E1 nets. Every E1 test potential is integrable against mixed E1 measures. If φ0∈PSH(ω0) is integrable against the limiting mixed measure and all potentials decrease to the specified limits, then the corresponding weighted measures converge weakly.

BJ7.27, 7.40, 7.44 and 7.45: On a reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, for ω ample and E1(ω) potentials, I is nonnegative, J and I are comparable, and I satisfies a quasi-triangle inequality. Finite-energy MA is local under maxima on the set where one potential is strictly larger; consequently ∫_{φ<ψ}MA(φ)≥∫_{φ<ψ}MA(ψ), and I(φ,ψ)=I(φ,max(φ,ψ))+I(max(φ,ψ),ψ). These assertions do not require EP.

BJ9.20: For a reduced irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an ample class ω, a Radon probability measure μ has finite dual energy sup_{φ∈E1(ω)}(Eω(φ)−∫φ dμ) if and only if every φ∈E1(ω) is μ-integrable.

BJ5.11: For an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and θ∈N1(X), EP for θ is equivalent to compactness of {φ∈PSH(θ):supφ=0} in the divisorial pointwise topology, and to convergence in PSH(θ) of every bounded-above increasing net.

BJ9.15–9.19: For a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, an ample class ω, and a finite-dual-energy probability measure μ, J(φ) is bounded by a dimensional constant times Jμ(φ)+E∨(μ), so maximizing nets have eventually bounded J. Any convergent net φ_i→φ in PSH(ω) with eventually bounded J converges to φ in L1(μ).

BJ8.3, 8.5 and 9.11: For a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an ample class ω, the outer energy E↓ is increasing and satisfies E↓(u+c)=E↓(u)+c. For φ∈E1(ω) and fixed f∈PL_R(X), E↓(φ+tf)=Eω(φ)+t∫f MAω(φ)+O(t²), with a constant uniform in φ. Under EP, this outer energy equals Eω(Pω(φ+tf)). For every finite-dual-energy probability measure μ, the MA measures of every maximizing E1 net converge weakly to μ.

BJ10.4 and 10.6: For an equidimensional reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an ample class ω, equality of the MA measures of two E1(ω) potentials is equivalent to I=0 and to their difference being locally constant. If u∈PSH(ω), v∈E1(ω), and u≤v almost everywhere for MAω(v), then u≤v everywhere. Neither assertion requires EP.

BE7.12–7.14: On a projective scheme over a complete non-Archimedean field, including a trivially valued field, every psh metric defined by decreasing fixed-bundle FS approximation on a semiample rational line bundle is a decreasing limit of smooth semipositive metrics on that same bundle. For a continuous metric the approximation is uniform. Smooth regularized FS metrics permit arbitrary real finite weights.

BE8.3(iv) and 8.4–8.5: On a projective scheme over a complete non-Archimedean field, smooth mixed Monge–Ampère measures, including the analytic fundamental cycle, commute with pushforward under every complete field extension. On fixed rational line bundles the operator has a unique extension to continuous psh-regularizable metrics, continuous for uniform convergence of metrics and weak convergence of measures; semipositive inputs give positive measures with mass equal to the mixed intersection number.

BE8.18 and BJ7.23: The analytic Deligne pairing of model metrics on actual generic-fiber line bundles equals the metric induced by their model Deligne pairing. For continuous ample-class psh potentials on a reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, the resulting continuous CLD/BE Monge–Ampère operator agrees with the BJ energy-pairing operator, without assuming EP.

BJ13.1, continuous-obstacle case: For a reduced irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, an ample class ω with EP, and f∈C0(X^an), ψ=Pω(f) is continuous and ω-psh, and ∫(f−ψ)MAω(ψ)=0. In particular f=ψ almost everywhere for MAω(ψ).

BJ5.17 and 5.9: For an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an ample class ω, EP is equivalent to continuity of Pω(f) for every continuous obstacle f; under EP these envelopes are genuine ω-psh potentials. If θ is a limit of classes θ_j≥θ having EP, then θ has EP.

BJ5.13: Let π:Y→X be a birational morphism of projective varieties over an algebraically closed trivially valued field. If θ∈N1(X) is the limit of a sequence θ_m such that θ_m−θ is ample and every θ_m has EP on X, then pullback PSH(X,θ)→PSH(Y,π*θ) is an onto homeomorphism in the divisorial pointwise topologies.
Stacks033G: If R→S is a faithfully flat ring map and S is normal, then R is normal.
Stacks0CEX: The property that a morphism is a universal homeomorphism is fpqc local on its target.

Stacks0BPZ: A local ring A is geometrically unibranch exactly when A_red is a domain, its integral closure A′ in its fraction field is local, and the residue field of A′ is purely inseparable over that of A.

Stacks035A and 035S: A scheme locally of finite type over a Nagata scheme is Nagata. The normalization of a Nagata scheme is finite. In particular these assertions apply to varieties over fields, since fields are Nagata.
Stacks30.17.2: If R is Noetherian, X and Y are proper over R, f:Y→X is finite and surjective, and L is an invertible sheaf on X, then L is ample if and only if f*L is ample.
Stacks10.50.2: For a field K and a local subring A⊂K, there exists a valuation ring with fraction field K dominating A.

Stacks15.125.2: If A⊂B is an injective local extension of valuation rings with fraction fields K⊂L and L/K finite, then both the residue extension and the value-group index are finite, and [Γ_B:Γ_A][κ_B:κ_A]≤[L:K].
